text_fidelity_a: Simmons Truplex .22 Mag Riflescope Even though the picture here for the silver variable is wrong (the real deal does have zoom adjustment ring), this scope is all kinds of right. For the money (and sometimes you can find it even lower) you get a fantastic little rimfire scope with coated lenses and included rings. Set it up on my 10/22 SS and the combo’s wicked fun. The windage and elevation adjustments are great, even though it’s hard to see on the black plastic which way it’s supposed to turn for what – easy fix, use some silver permanent marker to slightly highlight the raised letters and arrows. You don’t need any tools to do the adjustments, and the internal posts are good quality brass. The reticle is a simple 4 plex cross with no BDC holds or any other markings – it’s a point and shoot – for my rifle I set it at 50 yards and it’s spot on (1/2” group was the best I got out of 150 rounds first time with it at the range.) The zoom adjustment wheel is smooth and not too difficult to turn. The included dovetail rings are decent even though there’s no vertical center screw for recoil motion lock – again, this is for rimfire or lighter recoil. I wouldn’t (or I don’t even think it could) mount these on a picatinny rail, but they fit 11mm dovetail no problem. The silver color is a bit too shiny for my taste, that’s maybe my biggest hang-up. Overall, I’d buy again.
text_fidelity_b: Simmons Truplex .22 Mag Riflescope

Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack, Model ZN102, Black This is a good bicycle carrier, though could be improved. This was used to transport two “adult” and one “women's” bicycles for a 2000 mile move on the back of a Kia Forte 5 Door hatchback. The bicycles were secured with bungee cords to keep the handle bars from moving.

Some reviewers pointed out that it's difficult to put three bicycles on this rack, I didn't have this issue because in my case one of the bikes had a different geometry from the other two. If you have three bicycles with identical geometry this might be an issue though.

Don't underestimate how tight the straps need to be. On the Kia Forte 5 door there is no way to attach the bottom straps to the bumper cover. I had to attach both of the bottom straps to the tow hook on the metal frame of the bumper on the driver side. After the first 500 miles, one of the bottom straps loosed up which made the rack rock side to side which caused the passenger side lateral strap to slide down and scratch the paint. After I put in some effort in re-tightening the straps the rack stayed in place for the next 1500 miles. While I suspect that if the straps are tight the car paint will be safe, I do wish that the hooks had some kind of soft rubber coating.

Except for the paint scratch from the strap hook, the rack fared well.
text_fidelity_b: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack, Model ZN102, Black

text_fidelity_a:
ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH I often have three or 4 different workout groups going on at the same time and I have two of the older model 740MX watches and two of the newest AX740's to help me manage it all. What I like best about this watch is that after hitting the split button which I do at the beginning of every repeat in a set, I can hit the release button and the watch will show BOTH the Total Running Time AND the running repeat time. So if I am running a set of 100's on 1:20 I hit the split button at every 1:20, then hit the release button, it shows me the running repeat time so that I can eyeball the splits during the repeat and I can shout out times as they are coming in. It also shows the number of repeats so that I never lose count of the number of repeats. So with multiple groups and multiple watches it really helps me stay organized and allows me to give better feedback to the swimmers. I have had the two 740MX's for 10 years now and have used them nearly every day and often twice a day. Recently one or the other will blank out occassionally so I have purchased the newer AX740. I am not mentioning the blanking out as a problem but more of a testament that they have lasted this long under heavy use.

These are also wonderful watches for swim meets especially when you have the luxury of one watch per swimmer. Hit the split, write it down (or let the memory save it for later), hit release and see the total running time as well as the split running time.

If there is one drawback to this watch, it's that reset is made by holding down the start button for 2 seconds -- which seems like forever when you are trying to run a bunch of individuals doing one at a time 25's and you want to get ready for the next swimmer NOW. The older versions had a similar reset but it was about 1.3 seconds, the newer AX740 is a full 2 seconds. Sometimes I think my older watches are beginning to fail because I hold down the split button as hard as I can wishfulling thinking that it will speed up the reset. A light touch does the same and may lead to a longer life of the watch.
text_fidelity_b: ACCUSPLIT AX740 PRO MEMORY (50) DUAL LINE STOPWATCH

-If you don't have a tall nose, it might be hard to squeeze to pop your ears
-Nose area could use a more flexible plastic to make the aforementioned problem less of a problem

Recommendation:
-Prep the mask before you use it for the first time by rubbing toothpaste on both sides of the lens and rinse with water, this will remove the protective film it came with. It might be a good idea to do it a couple of times.
-Right before entering the water, wet the mask and rub dish detergent on the inside of the lens and rinse again. This will keep it from fogging while you are underwater.

I usually drink two 32-oz bottles of something every day -- usually water and/or a favorite Crystal Light mix. So I was interested to try out this Bubba tumbler.

I like the design -- a basic tumbler shape, silicone sleeve, flexible rubber-ish straw, tight-fitting lid. It's not spill-proof: the straw is inserted into a hole in the middle of the lid that has a small "divot" to allow air into the sealed tumbler so that you can sip. The straw fits nicely into the hole, but the divot leaves an opening for liquid to escape. Since I'm not very hard on my water bottles, I don't consider this a problem. I'm not prone to dropping or tipping them, so there shouldn't be a problem with spillage.

The sleeve provides *some* insulation so that my drink does stay colder longer than a non-insulated bottle, but not as long as a vacuum bottle. I hand-wash mine -- it's just something I do each night before I go to bed -- so I don't need to deal with removing and replacing the sleeve.

For the price, I think it's a good deal. I'm planning to purchase another one or two to have spares, and I'm definitely taking one of them along on my upcoming travels.

text_fidelity_a:
ABUS Mini Ultra 410 Bike U-Lock I really like this lock. I have not had any of the defective shackle problems that some other reviewers are writing about; I hope that they were able to return the product for a replacement or refund. My shackle slides easily onto the U portion. It also slides on in either direction (the keyhole has to face down, but either end of the U slides easily into either hole). These mini-U-locks are great if you always lock your bike to a modern bike rack, which should be designed so the mini-U lock fits easily. The lock fits around the bike rack, my front wheel, and the frame, then you can use a cable or another lock around the rear wheel. The lock is too small to fit around a parking meter, but I never do that now that my city has bike racks all over the place. These mini-U locks are much lighter weight and easier to carry than the full-sized U-locks. This lock only comes with 2 keys so don't lose them (other brands include 3 or 5 keys with their locks). I would prefer a metal bike mount, but this plastic one hasn't failed on me yet. I do like the way the you lock the lock to the mount so it is very secure (no way for it to fall off when you are riding).

This lock has a Sold Secure silver rating, which is done by a well known independent European bike lock testing program. Some locks have a gold rating, but those are all much more expensive and much heavier than this one. A gold-rated lock is appropriate if you lock your bike for long periods of time on the street in a big city with a known bike theft problem (like San Francisco or New York City).

While this lock works great, I'm giving it only 4 stars because there are only 2 keys and also because the comparable OnGuard Bulldog mini-U-lock costs much less on Amazon (and comes with 5 keys).
text_fidelity_b: ABUS Mini Ultra 410 Bike U-Lock

text_fidelity_a:
SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos Let's say that you are confronted by an attacker who demands something of value from you. You whip out your "police strength" red pepper get and hit him full in the face even though he is still eight feet away. After a second or two, he begins to laugh and keeps coming at you. What went wrong? The spray deployed exactly as you tested it, yet this guy seemed immune. It was made by a reputable company. And all the reviews you read were extremely positive. But what no one bothered to do was to test the formula on themselves.

Test this on myself? What kind of stupidity is this? Think of it this way. Would you buy a gun and depend on it to defend yourself and/or your family without testing it previously? Of course not. The problem here is that it's easy to test guns, knives, clubs and other weapons by hitting something with it and assessing the damage. No one gets hurt and yet you can become very comfortable by mastering the proper delivery and seeing the expected results. But pepper spray is another matter entirely. No one in their right mind wants to spray themselves in the face. Certainly not the first 21 reviewers of this product. They all seemed to be perfectly happy that the spray deployed as advertised. No offense to any of them but some of you might end up trusting your lives to this product.

But it's really pretty easy to test on yourself. I was a product development manager for a small defense corporation about 40 years ago. I had to vouch for any product that we developed and sold. Putting a defective product in the hands of someone who truly needed it (even back then) would result in a substantial lawsuit. One of the items we developed and eventually sold was one of the first self defense sprays available to the average consumer. We would pay volunteers to take a full shot in the face as we developed and improved the formula. When we began production there was always the problem of if the canisters were filled with the proper formula. Since I was unwilling to shoot myself in the face while randomly sampling dozens of these units, I would test out the sprayer on the back of my hand.

If you want to truly rely on this product, here is what you need to do. Find a sheltered (from the wind) outdoor area away from people and animals. Your back should be toward any (even) minor breeze. Hold your left hand out from your body, unfasten the safety trigger, and shoot a small stream onto the back of your hand. Hold your breath while doing so and then step away from any residual mist. Your hand should have a large orange spot on it and you should immediately feel a strong tingling or burning sensation on the back of your hand. There were no instructions that I could find that told you to shake the canister first -- so I didn't.

Unfortunately nothing happened! No stinging or burning. Even though I was just recovering from a bad cold, I put my nose within an inch of the formula and took a quick sniff. Nothing! I tried the whole exercise again after this time shaking the canister first. The results? A more consistent mixture on the back of my hand, but again no deterrent that I could detect. With my damaged and tender nose and still sore throat, i would have been expecting discomfort of an epic nature. So my guess is that this particular canister was faulty. On the other hand, no other reviewer has tested this on themselves to corroborate my findings. Perhaps the company will contact me to try and figure out why it doesn't work. This isn't my first rodeo, but it is my only shot at life. If this product failed me at the only time I really needed it, I wouldn't be around to ask for a refund.

NOTE: There was a direct sale company (We Care America) back in the late 1970's that also sold a personal defense spray. 60 Minutes (or some other news program) proved on a televised segment that the spray didn't work as advertised, taking what was once a viable company into bankruptcy. Thousands of those canisters were sold to people who believed that they were going to be adequately protected by WCA's product. That's when I knew that I had to test these things for myself.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Runner Pepper Gel, Maximum Police Strength OC Spray, Reflective Hand Strap for Easy Carry & Quick Access, 35 Bursts, Secure & Easy to Use Safety, Optional Clip-On Alarm & LED Armband Combos

text_fidelity_a:
CamelBak Podium Chill Insulated Bike Water Bottle 21 oz, Teal I am an avid cyclist and have a lot of the older camelbak podium series bottles which were great but also somewhat annoying because the valve had a tendency to get moldy quickly (especially if you use gatorade or other sugary sport drink mixes), and the valve assembly was quite difficult to disassemble for cleaning.

The new redesigned camelbak valve on these is a huge improvement over the older ones, they seem to be more resistant to getting moldy in the first place.. and if they do it is quick and easy to disassemble for cleaning! Great job camelbak!

My only qualm with these bottles is that the plastic is very soft and gets marred/scratched very easily. This was kind of the case with the older camelbak bottles also but it seems even worse on these newer ones. It doesn't affect the function of the bottles so its not a huge issue but just kind of annoying that these look old and beat up after one or two rides whereas I have some other (non-camelbak) bottles that are several years old and still look practically new. That said, those other bottles use harder plastic which is more rigid and more difficult to squeeze, making them harder to drink from, and the ease of squeezing out a large amount of liquid is what makes the camelbak bottles so great, so its a tradeoff I'm willing to make..

I've noticed some reviewers complaining about them not fitting well in bottle cages but I've never had issues on any of my bikes, I use arundel cages on most of them but I have also have some specialized and lezyne cages.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Podium Chill Insulated Bike Water Bottle 21 oz, Teal

3D Fitness Tracker & Real Time Audio Coach, Moov Now:Swimming Running Water Resistant Activity Calories Tracker with Sleep Monitor, Bluetooth Smart Wristband for Android and iOS, Stealth Black First thing that I loved about this Moov Now is that I don't have to take it off and plug it in to be recharged every day. Nice to just change out a watch battery after months of use. This is so small and light weight that I barely knew I was wearing it. I'm sure after the "newness" of having it on wears off I won't even remember I have it on.
Download the needed app for you phone and you're set.
Comes with a large and small strap that can easily be changed out.
After you pick out what training routine you'll be doing at that time, tap the top of the Moov to connect it via Bluetooth. Then you can choose your level of difficulty. What's nice is that if Moov feels that you can do a higher intensity, after you've finished a routine, it will let you know.
I like to listen to music while I work out. Can still do this with the Moov Now. A female voice that talks and helps you through the workout only lowers the music volume when she needs to update you about something.
What is really nice about this fitness tracker is that it helps with my workout that no other fitness tracker, that I've owned so far, has done.
With my walking and running. I like that it lets me know when I wasn't running properly. Coached me to land softer on my feet and to take longer strides. The "Run & Walk" category has the most workouts to choose from so far. Has five to choose from: Running Efficiency, Speed Endurance, Brisk Walking, Sprint Intervals, and Open Training. Selecting one brings you to yet another page that is specific for that training where more details can be read along with highlighted traits of that workout like cardio, lean muscle, or low impact. Can't filter activities with these highlights but, they are a good way to determine whether a workout will address the goals you want.
It does have a LE-enabled heart rate monitor but, I haven't tried to use that part of this fitness tracker yet.
I can't wait to try all the other work out options it has. Even more excited to see all the other work out routines the developers can come up with and add to the app.
This week I'll be working out at the gym so will be trying that work out app at that time.
All the work out activity apps are: running, walking, cycling, swimming, and gym routines.
I love how it will show me how much activity I've done that day. A little kick in the pants on the days I feel a little lazier especially when it will tell me how long I spent just sitting on my tush. But, I'm not working to join the olympic team. I'm just a man that is starting to look at his body and decided to hit the gym every so often.
I just love how I have a small personal trainer that pushes me a little more than I would push myself. And, it's all done privately in my ears while I'm listening to motivational music.
When you are all done, the Moov shows the history of your work out. It is easily accessed from the App homepage. Tap each individual workout to see all the recorded stats and all the levels you've completed. There is a lot of information that the device records for each workout. Really interesting to look at and really helpful where there are routines with a variety of different moves.
And, any support I may need, I can email Moov directly at support@moov.cc. If they are willing to help people directly in here, where we are making our reviews, it shows that they will probably be right there for you when you contact them directly. Kudus to you at support!!

What a great great Fitness Tracker this Moov Now is. So unique and easy to use.
Because the price is so reasonable, this will be a great gift that I can get for all my friends that work out. Even a better gift for the 2 friends that I have that are really into swimming.

It is made out of extremely thin and flexible material. It can fold up into itself and zip up (see picture) for easy storage and transport when not using it to carry items in. I can see this bag as being an excellent option for travelers who might find themselves needing another bag/storage option at the last minute. Like when you realize at the airport your bag is overweight and to avoid a huge baggage fee, you wish you had a small bag you could put some heavy items in and carry it on the plane instead. This would be perfect for that. Or you spend the holidays with relatives and they send you home with more goodies for the kids than you have room in your luggage for.

It's not a primary use bag. There is no padding at all. Not in the bottom of the bag. Not in the shoulder straps. There is no protection for items within the bag or your shoulders. It would not be comfortable carrying this with anything substantial or heavy inside. The material reminds me of an inexpensive windbreaker or poncho.

Pros:
Great backup bag for unexpected situations
Lightweight and very compact
Folds and zips into itself for easy storage and transport

Cons:
Flimsy shoulder straps with no padding
Questionable ability to carry heavy, rigid items like books or glass bottles
No padding in the bag itself, thus no protection for items inside

I received this bag for minimal cost in exchange for my unbiased review.

text_fidelity_a: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag First of all, I used to be one of those people who thought trekking poles were for wusses, but as I've gotten a bit older and wiser I have found that they are indispensable for longer hikes. I can hike twice as far with them and they really help with some challenging up and downs. These poles look great and are comfortable to use.  I went on one 10 mile hike when I first used them. I did find that the pole adjustment locks took some getting used to.  You have to turn a knob and then flip the clip to lock it into position. If you tighten the screw too much then there is too much tension and you can't flip the clip, so you have to go back and loosen the screw a bit more and then try again. Once I got the hang of it, it was fairly simple. I would suggest doing it before you leave the house. I'd also suggest leaning hard on each pole to be sure it's locked firmly.  Also, when putting the mud guards on, it helps to screw them on to the threads at the pole bases and then push on firmly. I lost one mudguard (in some really deep mud.) The Foxelli company's customer service is excellent though and they sent a replacement pair out right away!  These come with a nice bag and two sets of tips (one for storage and one for asphalt) and two sets of guards (one for dirt and one for snow.)
text_fidelity_b: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a: Tenzing TZ 720 Lumbar Pack (AP Camo) Let me start by saying that I researched literally dozens of fanny packs before settling on this one. Badlands,Fieldline, LL Bean, ALPS, Allen, Timberhawk, Browning, Cabelas .  .  . you get the picture. I use a fanny pack primarily to run and gun longbeards and to get my archery gear into my hunting locations with a Summit Open Shot Climber on my back. This pack replaces an old fleece 380 cubic inch Fieldline that served me well for many years, but was always just a tad too small.  I can tell you that there are a limited number of packs available that are between what I consider to be too small at 450-500 cubic inches, and for me, too large at over 1000 cubic inches. I don't carry enough gear to require backpack type straps, nor do I want the complications associated with them. Furthermore, many  of the packs that DO tend to fall inside this capacity range  have what I call a "hopper" style zippered opening, which to me makes absolutely no sense. You unzip it and your gear rolls out. I want a top loading pack that retains my gear. If I've just climbed 20' , gotten settled in, unzip my pack and all my gear falls to the ground, well, lets just say I'm not a happy camper. This is a nicely designed pack that met the majority of my parameters developed over 40 years of hunting. This pack, in my opinion, is the perfect size. Enough room for all my gadgets and grub. The side straps "fold" easily and stay "folded" for  easy placement at the back of my platform. Lashing straps top and bottom, check. Plenty of zippered organizing compartments, check. Side strap pockets that actually have some capacity, check.  Oh. . Did I mention this is a great looking pack?  Which leads us to one of my few negatives. The attractive green panels that you see on the front and top of the pack as well as  the entire pack bottom are Dyneema, a super strong synthetic fiber material. Noisy??  Not terribly. Tenzing claims these panels are used for durability, and while I'm fairly certain this pack will indeed outlive my remaining years in the field, they are . . well . . synthetic.  While in my application it means little, if I were using this pack primarily  to stalk or still hunt, it might impact my choice. Get one in your hands and see for yourself. text_fidelity_a:
TIMBUK2 Command Laptop Backpack, Black [[VIDEOID:mo363W3UY9IZ8Y3]]Let me start by saying that I've been using various Timbuk2's bags since the mid 1990s. While the prices may be a bit high, I've consistently found their bags to be well built, durable, with excellent water protection. In fact, I recently used one of their camera backpacks on a three week trip across Japan where the bag was subjected to a number of downpours; no water ever pierced the bag's envelope.

In terms of size, the volume of this bag is comparable to the laptop briefcases that came with laptops in the 1990s through the early aughts. As you'll see in my video, the laptop is housed in a compartment on the back of the bag in a heavily padded sleeve. In the video I have a 13" MacBook Pro in it.

There are two other compartments for storage and numerous small zipper pockets. On one side there is a water bottle holder, and on one of the shoulder straps a bottle opener (a standard feature of all Timbuk2 bags).

There's heavy padding on the back of the bag (where your back touches it) as well as on the shoulder straps.

As the the video shows, it's not a large bag, and that's the point. It's meant to hold your laptop and several documents -- whatever you may need to bring home from work for the night or the weekend. It's also small enough that if you're going out after work and you have it with you, it will easily fit under a table. And, it will fit under any airplane seat.

Finally, I also like that there's no indication that it's a laptop bag. In fact, if someone were going through it, they probably wouldn't even notice the laptop compartment in the back.
text_fidelity_b: TIMBUK2 Command Laptop Backpack, Black

I have certainly used other "non-smart" bottles that feel better in my hands. The cap is functional, though I would have preferred a type of cap that has a spout or similar mechanism. For example, I love the Zojirushi cap that (1) keeps any parts where you place your lips clean (WATERH does that), (2) can be operated with one hand (WATERH does NOT do that; you need a hand to hold the bottle and the second one to open the cap), and (3) is easy to clean (the WATERH cap has some tight spaces that are hard to clean).

The bottle has a water sensor inside, as well as some kind of scales at the bottom of the bottle that helps the app determine how much water you have consumed. The bottle needs to be charged by resting it on a USB-C base charger, included with the product. I've been using the water bottle for a couple of days, and the bottle battery is at 97%, so apparently it will last quite long.

The bottle has a led ring near the base that reminds you when to drink. The led light is also used to display when the bottle is charging, when it is fully charged, etc.

The application is pretty basic and bare bones. The Apple Store display pretty bad customer reviews. I haven't found it to be bad. The only missing feature that is important to me is an automatic connection with Apple's Health application. Adding that feature would make much more useful to me.

The manufacturer states that "WaterH is equipped with a built-in TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) sensor meter so you can know exactly what's in your bottle. Stop guessing the quality of your water through taste or smell." The sensor is likely there, but I have found not way to access those results. There are no instructions, and exploring the app yielded nothing.

Bottomline: the WATERH water bottle is a fun gimmick, but not really necessary. Regardless of how you do it, drink plenty of water.
text_fidelity_b: WATERH Smart Water Bottle - Tracks Hydration Intake, Analyzes TDS Water Quality, LED Glow Reminder via Bluetooth. Hack Your Hydration Health, 18 oz

There are substantial price differences. This swivel version retails for about $60 while the high back is roughly half the price at $34. They both have the same level of comfort (which is passable) and take the same amount of time to assemble (a few minutes to set up and break down). I ultimately would recommend the cheaper version as, clearly, it is half the price and offers the exact same things, unless being able to turn around in circles is a priority for you.

I do enjoy the fact that this can be broken down and stored in a bag. Although it takes more time to put together than your typical camping chair, it’s worth it for it to be compact. Getting the corners of the chair into the poles isn’t incredibly difficult, but it does take some elbow grease; I assume this will become easier with time. I do think having the drink pocket on the front of the chair is a design flaw and the sides of the chair actually come up a bit high to be comfortable for your arms. It swivels incredibly well but again, is that a priority for most people? I don’t really think so. Also, as other reviewers have mentioned, it is a bit wobbly.

Overall, nice idea, but other versions of the chair are better. I particularly like the high back version because it has a pillow which supports your neck and the sides of the chair do not come up as high which is more comfortable.

I value my time greatly and hence I bought online. In this case my best option is to lick my wounds, buy another rod from a other brand and give warning to other potential buyers.

Scuba Choice Diving Stainless Steel Heavy Duty Multi-Purpose Dive Reel 290ft I own a Borzoi puppy and do not have a fenced in yard so I've trained him to run/frolic on 100-200 ft ropes (500 lb paracord from Home Depot). After several months of it getting wrapped around my legs and giving me severe rope burns and scars and spending 15-20 minutes several times a day detangling it to get started, I looked for a reel to use. I tried cheap large plastic extension cord reels and two types of dive reels. This one is the heaviest, best made, with best features. My plan was to remove the dinky rope from this and replace it with the thin paracord but, though the rope fits through the feeder slot, the paracord is such a bigger diameter than what comes with this that less than half the line fit on the real itself so it doesn't work for my use. It's a real shame because nothing else is as easy to use/control. It's possible I could find some really high tensile strength rope that's a smaller diameter but it's probably out of my price range.

The string that came with this lasted a few weeks til it just up and snapped when the rope was stuck on a branch and my puppy took off (at the time it broke he weighed about 45 lbs and now he's over 60 and half grown).

The hand grip is comfortable, hard, but easy to use. The slide lock has 3 settings- stop, go with clicks, and full out go. The clip hardware is fine, I'd probably trust it (strength wise) when my dog is full sized I just don't like the clip type (easy to accidentally unclip so not safe for a dog that's bred to take off and not come back easily).
text_fidelity_b: Scuba Choice Diving Stainless Steel Heavy Duty Multi-Purpose Dive Reel 290ft

text_fidelity_a:
Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue I’m torn with how to rate this chair. I have the 360 swivel version ($60) as well as this one, which is about half the price. This compaclite chair has a higher back which makes it more comfortable than the swivel version, and the pillow actually is a nice plus. It’s compact and more comfortable than typical folding chairs. When compared to the swivel version, this one wins no contest. However, it still isn’t enough for it to be bumped up to 5 stars, and I’ll tell you why.

As many others have mentioned, these chairs aren’t the sturdiest and wobble a bit. The drink holder is placed in an awkward place on the chair (right between your legs) and the chair does take a few minutes to set up, whereas a simple folding chair is done in a few seconds. I imagine this will get better with time, but it does take some elbow grease to get the corners of the chair into the poles. Although the pillow is quite comfortable and really nice, it makes folding the chair a bit more of a pain that the swivel version (because no pillow). One of compaclite’s best features is the fact that…yes…it’s compact, so the pillow adds a stressor that makes it difficult to be easily compact. I struggled for a solid 5 minutes to get this one in the bag.

Ultimately, it comes down to what you value. Do you need something that turns in a circle? Do you want arm rests? Do you want a pillow? Should it be compact? Do you want something that can be easily set up? If you are searching for a compact chair that can easily be carried and don’t mind set-up and break down times, then I would recommend this chair. Otherwise, you might want to look elsewhere if those aren’t your priorities.
text_fidelity_b: Compaclite High Back Oversize Steel Portable Chair for Outdoor Camping / Picnic / Hiking / Bicycling / Fishing / BBQ / Beach / Patio with Carry Bag, Royal Blue

Prevention The Toning Transformation: Firm Up, Lose Weight and Feel Amazing - Easy to Follow Strength and Toning at-Home Workout Videos! The set of this program is so well designed. It looks like a living room so you will feel right at home. The instructor, Sarah Kusch, has a pleasing personality and uses humor to motivate you into action. The creative exercises are fun and invigorating, making this a total body toning program you want to keep doing day after day! You will be excited as each new day brings workouts that increase the challenge.

After some of the longer 20-plus minute workouts you may feel like you want extra stretching. Some days only take 6 minutes, while others take 27 minutes.

One thing perfectionists will notice is that sometimes the instructor talks about variations or gives helpful tips and you have to be disciplined enough to continue on doing what you are supposed to be doing. It gets easy after a while to follow along or modify for lower or higher intensities. I also suggest counting on each side to make sure you are doing an even number.

Here is what the exercises are and how I felt about each workout or stretching routine:

Fit and Firm Foundations (27:30 minutes) – This workout has lots of repetitions so you will really feel the burn. There is a warm up and a stretch at the end. You will really work your core. The second time I did this I really felt it. The exercises you will be doing include: lateral leg lifts, side-angle leg lifts, lateral and front arm raises, deadlifts, half-circle leg lifts, lat pull down with a hand towel, triceps pulse and chops with a towel.

Standing Core Stability (6 minutes) – This is intensive core training focusing mostly on the abs. You will be lifting weight over your head.

Full Body Recharge (6 minutes) – This is a total body stretching routine that you will wish was even longer. My one cat usually insists I do more stretches after I'm done. He wants me to do cat pose and loves it when I do this routine.

Sweat and Strengthen (22:12 minutes) – This is cardio with low and high impact options. If you like HIIT you will enjoy doing intense exercises followed by exercises with weights. To be honest it keeps you invigorated and out of breath and I was doing the easiest variations to start. The exercises include speed skater, squat curl presses, triceps kickback, jumping jack with modifications, overhead reach, squat with forward punch, high knees, side-to-side squat, palms forward row, out-and-in taps, x arms, reach with tap back, biceps curls and squat reaches.

Total Body Tone (23 minutes) – This is really tough the first time you do it if you are over 50! You have to be able to get down on the floor and lay on your back. Which sounds easy unless you realize that getting back up is going to be a big effort. My lower back felt these exercises. Fortunately you can do the exercises at your own pace. You don't need to get off the floor quickly at any point. Some of these exercises are inspired by Pilates so you know they work. The exercises include: squat with overhead raise, bent-over row, overhead triceps extension, alternating forward lunge, reverse fly, wide squat with biceps curl, chest fly, triceps burnout, side leg lift, forearm plank, back extension on stomach, pelvic tilt and tabletop leg drop.

Tighten and Tone Basics (23:44 minutes) – It is best if you watch this one first before you try these exercises. There is a figure eight with weights, standing torso twists with weights, biceps curls, a sit-and-stand squat, reverse standing leg lifts, T fly, rainbow, triceps v and overhead chop. There is a cool down and stretching segment. I felt this weight training with cardio in my lower back but not badly. Felt this in my triceps too after doing it several times.

Belly Burn (7:25 minutes) – The exercises start with cat pose and move to bird dog, side plank, leg drops, forearm plank, back extensions and scissors. Sarah Kusch does not give a lot of time to move from one posture to another. Obviously she is not over 50! So this was challenging.

Tension Tamer (6:55 minutes) – After doing this the first time I decided to do Full Body Recharge in its place in the future. It actually increased my tension because of having to be on the floor. These stretches are good for the 20s, 30s and 40s. After 50 not so much. It is getting down on the floor that is the problem. There is a bridge hold, a Figure 4, hamstring stretch, child's pose. These look easy until you try to do them.

Power Sculpt (22 minutes) – This starts with good mornings and then squats, overhead reaches side to side, biceps curls, leg lifts and overhead presses. There is a tricky curtsy lunge with a punch, a rotation row and a reverse lung with lateral raise. You move on to a standing side crunch, upper back butterfly swimmers and lateral lunch. A donkey kick then changes to pulses and a side lift. There are alternate leg circles which provide a challenge and a marching bridge which is advanced. It ends with plank. Whew! This is a bit intense on the knees when you are down on the ground so you may want a padded mat. I could not do the marching bridge or the leg circles. I may get to them eventually when feeling stronger. Instead I just did some stretches while I watched. The end of this workout was my least favorite part of the workouts.

Fat Burning Fix ( 22:12) – This workout has a warm up and stretching at the end. It is cardio alternating with strength moves. It is for beginner, intermediate or advanced depending on which exercises you decide to follow. There is a diagonal slide, biceps lifts, triceps pulses, knee smashes, triceps kickbacks, lateral raises (a coordination challenge), a unique Genie Fly, step back lunge, lateral shuffles, forward lunge with a chip, weighted star (creative balancing with weight), jumping jack, W press out and high knees. Overall very challenging and I needed to drink a lot of water. Out of all the workouts in this program, this was the most intense.

To be honest some days were harder than others. I loved the 6 minute days because they gave me a rest in between the more challenging workouts. Some days I almost didn't get in a workout but I swapped a few days moving the 6 minute workout to the 20 minute workout day then did the 20 minute workout the next day and so it all worked out. Staying on a program is interesting. I only made one change in the workout that I didn't like - so I just did another stretching workout on that day. I skipped working out for a few days after day 22 because I fell in my yard – OK was walking back from the mailbox and my shoe caught on the cement sidewalk. So felt a bit sore and took a day off and then another when my back hurt. I also did Power Sculpt on day 31 because I was impatient to get to that workout. The instructions say you can swap workouts around and I find that does work in some cases.

What did I notice after all these workouts?

Increased muscular strength in my daily tasks. Suddenly picking up a case of 35 water bottles was not as difficult. Folding laundry was a breeze.

Increased balance – I could turn quickly without feeling like I was going to fall over. Walking around the house I feel a bit like a race driver with a new vehicle!

Increased Body Awareness – Everything felt smooth and fluid when moving. I felt more at home in my body and could sense greater strength and mobility.

Increased Energy – Like a lot! I'm even sleeping less. I feel happier and more in control of my life.

So I'd say this has definite advantages. This comes with a little booklet so you can keep track of everything. I did the beginner workout plan and wrote down the date and checked off the workouts as I did them. That kept me very organized. I have made it up to day 31 and there are 56 days!

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Prevention The Toning Transformation: Firm Up, Lose Weight and Feel Amazing - Easy to Follow Strength and Toning at-Home Workout Videos!

text_fidelity_a:
Continental Hometrainer Folding Tire I spent too much time reading about trainer tires and couldn't get any solid sense of a consensus, even an internet consensus. The best I was able to do was notice that people endorsing this tire gave cogent arguments for why they liked it; so I figured at least good critical thought was filtering opinions on these.

My experience is that it works great on the trainer. I have no other trainer tire for comparison; but compared with a road tire (Specialized Turbo Pro) it is night and day better. It grips better (e.g. sprints), is quieter... I guess that's enough.

I did get a tire bead jack to install it, but after the valve failed on the antique tube I was using, I was able to get this tire re-seated with my fingers. So maybe just the first installation is hard?

If you are like I was, combing through endless, non-comparative reviews of trainer tires, STOP RIGHT NOW AND BUY THIS ONE. It works great. There may be one that is better by some criterion over a very long period of time, but there is nothing wrong with this tire. I can't imagine any improvement. It even costs less than a typical road tire.

More advice: I thought it was frivolous to assemble a wheel just for the trainer but now I regret not doing it sooner. They have very cheap, serviceable wheels - and great prices on better wheels - right here on Amazon. I recommend keeping a separate wheel for the trainer so there is no disincentive for switching back and forth between indoors/out - and maybe more importantly, no incentive for buying another bike.
text_fidelity_b: Continental Hometrainer Folding Tire

text_fidelity_a:
ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones We were so looking forward to receiving this hammock - but when it arrived, our hopes and dreams were dashed to the ground like refuse thrown into a gutter! The hammock took longer than expected to arrive - but not to worry-- we patiently checked Amazon tracking on a daily basis to see when the refreshment of lying on a soft, sturdy hammock whilst sipping a cocktail - would arrive at our door. After waiting on the edge of our plastic lawn chairs for two weeks, the big day finally arrived! The hammock was delivered by our friendly Amazon courier and shouts of joy could be heart resounding through the halls of our home! Two of our sons ceremoniously carried the long hammock box into the house like a wealthy Roman patron being carried through the streets on a litter. The box was opened and said hammock was unrolled like a precious scroll. Visions of hours spent snoozing under a canopy of trees danced in the heads of family members as they clamored to put this 'Object of 'Liesure and Rest' onto the stand that had carried our old, canvas, LL BEAN hammock. After 14 years of service, that good sanctuary had finally rotted away. (Actually, I wasn't home for this part, but I'm sure this is how it went.)

Our faithful and strong sons set the hammock up beneath towering Tulip Populars, wafting in the refreshing breeze and waited for me to come home hoping to unveil a pleasant surprise for the beloved mother. I arrived home, hot, sweaty and tired from a long day of horseback riding with my faithful steed. A persistent headache was pounding in my brain from hours of tracking desperados through the forests. (Ok, I was actually trying to catch up to my friends who had galloped away rather prematurely.) Anyway, as I slogged through the house, wilted and exhausted, my god-like son winked at me whilst ushering me through the back door to the paradise that awaited in the back yard.

THERE IT WAS! THE HAMMOCK for which I had been longing! I sat down on the side and stretched my battered frame onto the hammock like Cleopatra reclining under a gold-embroidered canopy dressed as Aphrodite, (but wearing riding boots and half-chaps).....only to discover that the hammock of my dreams was an imposter!!!! THIS WAS NO SOFT BED OF ROSES TO LIE ON! NO! IT FELT LIKE BAD CARPET ON THE WALLS OF A CHEAP MOTEL! I stifled my revulsion and tried to get comfortable but it was no use. The fabric wasn't fabric at all - it felt like plastic water bottles woven into a nightmarish tapestry by well-intentioned environmentalists! I leapt from this bed of vipers disgusted and disappointed. My family pleaded with me to give it another chance, saying "It's not so bad, we like it!" "Philistines!!!!" I retorted! " THIS. WILL. NOT. DO!" whilst gnashing my teeth to the best of my ability. To which they shrugged and got the box out of the trash so we could return it.

Postscript - If you want a comfy hammock made out of sunbrella fabric, you have to spend about $250 these days. I found one on Wayfair and now we are anxiously awaiting that one to be delivered. Cheers! :)
text_fidelity_b: ALGOMA 2781SPC Quick Dry Hammock, 13-Feet, Earth Tones

text_fidelity_a: WELLFAST Survival Straw, 4 Pack Personal Water Filter with Extension Hose, 2-Stage Upgraded Portable Purification Straws for Hiking, Travel, Emergency, Camping I don't know how many people have a go-bag, but I would say that it is important to have one as weather conditions can change our lives almost instantly, forcing us to leave our homes.  Flooding, tornadoes, fires - we've seen them on television.  People being rescued from their homes and having nothing with them.  That's why a go bag is perfect - you don't know where you will end up and having straws that can filter water in a place where the water has been compromised.  As small as these straws are, they can take up a small amount of space in a go bag, alongside a sleeping bag, a blanket, matches, a couple of candles - y'know, things that will make you somewhat comfortable in a bad situation.  Drinking water is a must so get these straws for that moment, that just in case time you need them.
text_fidelity_b: WELLFAST Survival Straw, 4 Pack Personal Water Filter with Extension Hose, 2-Stage Upgraded Portable Purification Straws for Hiking, Travel, Emergency, Camping
